test_title: PYST 20: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 13 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In the context of computer memory hierarchy, which of the following statements regarding access speed and cost per bit is generally true as you move from registers towards secondary storage?

options.text: Access speed increases and cost per bit decreases
Access speed increases and cost per bit increases
Access speed decreases and cost per bit decreases
Access speed decreases and cost per bit increases.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Access speed decreases and cost per bit decreases.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As we move down the memory hierarchy—from registers to secondary storage—the **access speed decreases**. Registers are the fastest, while secondary storage devices like hard drives are significantly slower.
 
• The **cost per bit of storage decreases** as we move from registers to secondary storage. Registers and cache are expensive due to their high-speed performance and small size.
 
• Registers are located within the CPU, offering **nanosecond-level access times**, whereas secondary storage devices like HDDs or SSDs have access times in milliseconds or microseconds.
 
• Secondary storage devices, such as hard drives, offer **much larger storage capacity** at a lower cost per bit but are slower in terms of data retrieval compared to primary memory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Memory Hierarchy in Computers**

 
 
• It refers to the arrangement of memory types based on **speed, cost, and capacity**.
 
• It typically includes registers, cache, main memory (RAM), and secondary storage (HDD/SSD).
 
• Registers and cache are the fastest but have the smallest capacity, while secondary storage is slower but offers large capacity.
 
 
 
• **Access Time**
 
 
• Access time is the time taken by the CPU to retrieve data from memory.
 
• Registers have the shortest access time, measured in nanoseconds, while secondary storage access time is measured in milliseconds or microseconds.
 
 
 
• **Cost per Bit**
 
 
• Cost per bit refers to the expense incurred for storing one bit of data.
 
• Registers and cache have the highest cost per bit, while secondary storage devices have the lowest cost per bit.
 
 
 
• **Secondary Storage**
 
 
• Includes devices like HDDs, SSDs, and optical disks.
 
• It is non-volatile and provides persistent storage for data even when the system is powered off.
 
 
 
• **Registers**
 
 
• Smallest and fastest memory located directly within the CPU.
 
• Used to temporarily store data that is actively being processed by the CPU.
